title: High-Protein Creamy Tuscan Chicken Skillet
description: This high-protein creamy Tuscan chicken skillet features tender chicken breasts in a rich garlic, sun-dried tomato, and spinach sauce. Ready in just 25 minutes, it delivers 35 grams of protein per serving. Save it for your next meal prep.

ingredients.note: substitute for yogurt to prevent curdling, or use full-fat Greek yogurt

steps: Season the chicken breasts evenly with 3/4 teaspoon of the salt and all of the black pepper.

Heat olive oil and 1 tablespoon of butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the chicken and sear for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). Remove chicken to a clean plate and set aside.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter to the same skillet. Add the minced garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly so the garlic does not burn.
Pour in the chicken broth to deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom, and let it simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Reduce the heat to low. Stir in the heavy cream and grated parmesan cheese, along with the remaining 1/4 teaspoon of salt, stirring until the cheese melts and the sauce is smooth and creamy.
Stir in the baby spinach and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted and bright green.
Return the cooked chicken and any resting juices back into the skillet, spooning the creamy sauce over the top, and heat through for 1 minute before serving.
tips: Let the Greek yogurt come to room temperature before whisking it into the warm broth to prevent curdling.
Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
storage: Keeps well in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave.

Sear the chicken in a hot skillet until fully cooked.

Whisk in broth, Greek yogurt, and parmesan for the sauce.
Stir in spinach until wilted, then add the chicken back.

issues: The salt quantity (1/2 tsp total for 1.5 lbs chicken and the sauce) is far too low and will result in bland chicken and sauce; standard test kitchen recipes use around 1 to 1.5 teaspoons of salt total.

Using plain 0% Greek yogurt directly in a hot pan with chicken broth risks curdling due to the lack of fat and low pH, even if tempered. Standard creamy Tuscan chicken recipes use heavy cream or whole milk/cream cheese, but if using Greek yogurt, it needs proper tempering or a stabilizing starch to prevent separation.
